justification: We are developing small, computationally efficient models to predict vegetation-fire behaviour, with the longer-term aim of helping prevent wildfires and improve wildfire risk reduction. This is simulation-based scientific research, not yet validated for operational wildfire decisions. We train and compare plain and soft-gated recurrent neural networks (approximately 5800 parameters) on 2080 preserved simulation histories, using fixed grouped training/validation/test folds. We request 2 GPUs total globally (one additional) for Google Batch FLEX_START. Google has already approved 3 preemptible NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 16 preemptible CPUs in us-central1, but the global limit of 1 prevents using that regional allowance. The first matched plain/gated pair took approximately 4 hours on one L4; remaining pairs have the same recipe, with actual runtime depending on validation stopping. Each Batch job has an 18.25-hour maximum task runtime and an 18.5-hour VM-age watchdog, and may wait up to 24 hours for allocation. We use immutable per-epoch checkpoints, verified optimizer/RNG resume checks, cloud supervision, cleanup, and no automatic paid retries. The cumulative experiment budget is USD125; launches are gated by the remaining budget. Please reconsider the minimum global increase to 2 for this delay-tolerant wildfire-prevention research workload.
